columns.name: ORDER_NUMBER
columns.description: This is a reference number for this order.

columns.name: PRIORITY
columns.description: This field contains the priority of the order that was received from OERR.

columns.name: NUMBER
columns.description: (Not currently used.)

columns.name: PATIENT_NAME
columns.description: This is the patient for which the medication has been ordered.

columns.name: PROVIDER
columns.description: This field should contain the prescribing physician's name.

columns.name: MED_ROUTE
columns.description: This is the route of administration for this medication.  (If acorresponding abbreviation is found for this route in the MEDICATIONROUTES file, this package will print that abbreviation on it's reports.)

columns.name: TYPE
columns.description: This identifies the type of medication ordered.

columns.name: SELF_MED
columns.description: This should contain a `1' (or `YES') if this medication is to beadministered by the patient to himself.

columns.name: HOSPITAL_SUPPLIED_SELF_MED
columns.description: This should contain a `1' (or `YES') if this medication is to be a`SELF MED' and this site's pharmacy is to supply the medication.  Thisis only asked if the user enters `YES' (or `1') to the SELF MED prompt.If the SELF MED field is ever edited to show `NO' (or `0'), this isautomatically deleted.

columns.name: SCHEDULE_TYPE
columns.description: This describes the type of schedule for the dispensing of themedication(s) that make up the order.  PRE-OP orders are usually considered to be ON-CALL orders, and ordersdispensed as MUTLI-DOSE CONTAINERS are usually considered to be FILL ONREQUEST orders.

columns.name: SPECIAL_INSTRUCTIONS
columns.description: This is any special instructions (using abbreviations whenever possible)needed for this order.  This would include the physician's reason forordering a PRN.  The abbreviations and expansions from the MEDICATIONINSTRUCTIONS file are utilized.

columns.name: RENEWAL
columns.description: (Not currently used.)

columns.name: START_DATE_TIME
columns.description: This is the date and time the order is to begin.  This package initially assigns the START DATE/TIME to the closest administration time or next admin. time or NOW depends on the value of the DEFAULT START DATE CALCULATION field in the INPATIENT WARD PARAMETERS file. START DATE/TIME may not be entered prior to 7 days from the order's LOGIN DATE.

columns.name: DAY_LIMIT
columns.description: This is the number of days that this order will last.

columns.name: DOSE_LIMIT
columns.description: This is the number of times the medication is to be administered.

columns.name: *UNITS_PER_DOSE
columns.description: This is now for use only by the package.  Units per Dose is now associatedwith each dispense drug.

columns.name: *PRE-EXCHANGE_UNITS
columns.description: This is the number of actual units needed for this order until the nextcart exchange.

columns.name: RENEWAL_USER
columns.description: This is the user who renewed this order, or marked this order to berenewed.

columns.name: VERIFYING_NURSE
columns.description: This is the nurse who verifies the order.

columns.name: DATE_VERIFIED_BY_NURSE
columns.description: This is the date the order was verified by the nurse.

columns.name: VERIFYING_PHARMACIST
columns.description: This is the pharmacist who verified the order.

columns.name: DATE_VERIFIED_BY_PHARMACIST
columns.description: This is the date the order was verified by the pharmacist.

columns.name: PHYSICIAN
columns.description: This is the physician who signed off on the order.

columns.name: DATE_VERIFIED_BY_PHYSICIAN
columns.description: This is the date the physician signed off on the order.

columns.name: CLERK
columns.description: This is the user who entered the order.

columns.name: DATE_ENTERED_BY_CLERK
columns.description: This is the date (to the second) that the order was entered.

columns.name: SOLUTION
columns.description: (Not currently used.)

columns.name: STOP_DATE_TIME
columns.description: This is the date and time the order will automatically expire.  Thispackage initially assigns a default STOP DATE/TIME, depending on the SITEPARAMETERS.

columns.name: SCHEDULE
columns.description: This is the frequency (ONLY) with which the doses are to beadministered.  Several forms of entry are acceptable, such asQ6H, 09-12-15, STAT, QOD, and MO-WE-FR@AD (where MO-WE-FR aredays of the week, and AD is the admin times).  The schedulewill show on the MAR, labels, etc.  No more than TWO spaces(Q3H 4, TID PC PRN, or Q4H PRN) in the schedule are acceptable.If the letters PRN are found as part of the schedule, no admintimes will print on the MAR or labels, and the PICK LIST willalways show a count of zero (0).  Avoid using notation such as W/F (with food) or WM (withmeals)in the schedule as it may cause erroneous calculations.That information should be entered into the SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS.  When using the MO-WE-FR@AD schedule, please remember thatthis type of schedule will not work properly without the '@'character and at least one admin time, and that at least thefirst two letters of each weekday entered is needed.

columns.name: ORDER_DATE
columns.description: This is the date the medication was ordered.

columns.name: LOG-IN_DATE
columns.description: This is the date (to the second) the ordered was entered.

columns.name: STATUS
columns.description: This is the status of the order.

columns.name: DATE_RENEWAL_MARKED
columns.description: This is the date the order was marked to be renewed.

columns.name: MARKED_CANCELLED
columns.description: This is an internal flag showing that the order has been marked tobe cancelled.

columns.name: MARKED_CANCELLED_USER
columns.description: This is the user who marked the order to be cancelled.

columns.name: INACTIVE_DATE_TIME
columns.description: This is the original stop date of the order, and is updated when theorder is cancelled.

columns.name: DOSES_CALLED_FOR
columns.description: This is the total amount of the medication to be dispensed as calculatedby the package.

columns.name: DOSES_ACTUALLY_DISPENSED
columns.description: This is the amount of the medication actually dispensed as entered bythe pharmacist.

columns.name: RETURNS
columns.description: This is the number of doses returned of this medication from the patient'scassette upon the termination of this order.

columns.name: TOTAL_RETURNS
columns.description: This is the total amount of returns for this order.

columns.name: TOTAL_UNITS_DISPENSED
columns.description: This is the total amount dispensed for this order, including PRE-EXCHANGENEEDS and EXTRA UNITS DISPENSED.

columns.name: DATE_MARKED_CANCELLED
columns.description: This is the date that the order was marked for cancellation.

columns.name: ADMIN_TIMES
columns.description: This is the set of administration times for this order.

columns.name: COMMENTS
columns.description: This is a word processing field that is purely informational.  Thisfield only shows on the expanded view on a order.

columns.name: FREQUENCY_(IN_MINUTES)
columns.description: This is either a code or the number of minutes between the administrationtimes for the order.

columns.name: TRANSFER
columns.description: This is an internal flag set if the order was cancelled due to thepatient being transferred.

columns.name: PV_FLAG
columns.description: This is an internal flag set if the order was ever verified by apharmacist.

columns.name: LABEL_DATE
columns.description: This is the date the last label record was created for this order.

columns.name: LABEL_REASON
columns.description: This is the last activity to take place on the order that created alabel record.

columns.name: NEW_ORDER_NO.
columns.description: When an order is first made active, the new order number (from ^PS(55)) isstored in this field.  (Not currently used.)

columns.name: SIG
columns.description: This is the provider's exact instructions for this order's medicationand its administration.

columns.name: PURGE_FLAG
columns.description: This is an internal flag set when the order is due to be purged (deleted).

columns.name: ORDERS_FILE_ENTRY
columns.description: This is the pointer value of the corresponding entry in the Orders file(100) when the order is entered through the OE/RR process.

columns.name: LAST_WARD
columns.description: This is the last ward the patient was located when the order expiredor was discontinued.  This is automatically updated by the Unit Dosepackage when the package finds that the patient is first admitted orwhen the patient is found to have been transferred.  This allows anyreturns that are entered to be credited to the correct ward.

columns.name: LABEL_CREATOR
columns.description: This is the user who took the action that created the label for thisorder.

columns.name: WARD_FOR_AUTO-CANCEL_LABEL
columns.description: This is the ward the patient was on before the transfer or dischargethat created the label occurred.

columns.name: IV_TYPE
columns.description: Type of IV - 'A' for Admixture, 'C' for Chemotherapy, 'H' for Hyperal,'P' for Piggyback, and 'S' for Syringe.

columns.name: CHEMOTHERAPY_TYPE
columns.description: A chemotherapy IV order may be one of three type: admixture, piggyback,or syringe.  The type of chemotherapy IV must be identified as one of thesetypes, so the system will know what kinds of questions to ask in order toproperly complete this order.

columns.name: SYRINGE_SIZE
columns.description: Enter the size of the syringe which is to be used to administer this IV.

columns.name: INTERMITTENT_SYRINGE
columns.description: A syringe IV order may be continuous or intermittent.  If a syringe typeis continuous (not intermittent), the same order entry procedure will befollowed as if a hyperal or admixture is being entered.  If a syringe orderis to be intermittent, the same order entry method as the piggyback typewill be followed.

columns.name: INFUSION_RATE
columns.description: The rate at which the IV is to be administered.  This value, togetherwith the total volume of the hyperal or the admixture type, is used todetermine the time covered by one bag; hence the system can predict thebags needed during a specified time of coverage.  This field is free textfor IVPB's.  For LVP's you must enter a number representing the infusionrate.  You may also specify the # of bags per day needed, which willbecome the default number of LABELS PER DAY.   Example.  125 = 125 ml/hr (IV system will calculate bags needed per day)          125@2 = 125 ml/hr with 2 labels per day      TITRATE@1 = TITRATE with 1 label per day. The format of this field is either a number only or [FREE TEXT@NUMBER OF LABELS PER DAY]. Note: If an administration time(s) is defined, the number of labels willreflect the administration time(s) for the IVPB type orders.For example:  One administration time of 12:00 is specified.  The infusionrate is entered as 125@3.  Only 1 label will print.

columns.name: SCHEDULE_INTERVAL
columns.description: Interval (in minutes) between administrations of the IV order.

columns.name: ATZERO
columns.description: If an IV order is intermittent and a schedule was entered in the formSCHEDULE@0.  Notice there are no spaces in the input.  When a schedule isentered in this form, this field is set to 1.  This causes the order to beprinted on the Ward and Manufacturing lists with 0 doses due.  Scheduledlabels for the order will not be printed unless the Ward list is updatedbefore printing scheduled labels.  This is a 'print on demand' functionsimilar to entering INFUSION RATE@0 for continuous orders.

columns.name: IV_ROOM
columns.description: IV room where IV bag was prepared for administration.

columns.name: REMARKS
columns.description: This is not displayed on IV labels, but is printed on some IV reports.

columns.name: OTHER_PRINT_INFO
columns.description: For use by Pharmacy to print additional information on IV labels andreports.

columns.name: PROVIDER_COMMENTS
columns.description: This is used to store an additional information the provider needs topass along to pharmacy or ward personnel when an order is entered/editedthrough OE/RR.

columns.name: PREVIOUS_ORDER_NUMBER
columns.description: When an order is created from an active order, the old number (from^PS(55)) is stored in this field.

columns.name: *PRIMARY_DRUG
columns.description: This is the primary drug associated with the order. If the order isa unit dose order all dispensed drugs entered must be matched to theorder's primary drug. If the order is an IV order at least one of theadditives or solutions entered must match the primary drug.

columns.name: *DOSAGE_ORDERED
columns.description: This is the amount of the medication the patient is to receive as onedose for this order.  This should be an amount with a unit of measure,such '500MG' or '50CC'.  THIS SHOULD NOT BE THE NUMBER OF TABLETS, ETC.

columns.name: REASON_ORDER_CREATED
columns.description: This is used to show the method used to create this order.

columns.name: PREVIOUS_ORDER
columns.description: If an action is taken on an order that causes a new order to be created,this will contain a code identifying the previous order.

columns.name: FOLLOWING_ORDER
columns.description: If an action is taken on an order that causes a new order to be created,this will contain a code identifying the order created.

columns.name: *NATURE_OF_ORDER
columns.description: This is the method the provider used to communicate to the user to enter(or take any other action) the order.

columns.name: REASON_FOR_FOLLOWING_ORDER
columns.description: If the order has been edited or renewed, this will contain the code corresponding to the action taken.

columns.name: ORDERABLE_ITEM
columns.description: This identifies the Orderable Item associated with the order. If the ordercontains multiple dispense drugs, or a single dispense drug requiringmultiple units/dose, the Orderable Item and Dosage Ordered fields will be displayed.

columns.name: DOSAGE_ORDERED
columns.description: This is the amount of the medication the patient is to receive as one dose for this order. This should be an amount with a unit of measure, suchas '500mg' or '50CC'. THIS SHOULD NOT BE THE NUMBER OF TABLETS, ETC.

columns.name: NATURE_OF_ORDER
columns.description: This is the method the provider used to communicate the order to the user to enter (or take any other action on) the order.

columns.name: INSTRUCTIONS
columns.description: INSTRUCTIONS

columns.name: CLINIC
columns.description: Entry must be a clinic.  Depending on the condition, INACTIVATE and REACTIVATE dates may exist.

columns.name: REQUESTED_START_DATE_TIME
columns.description: This is the Date/Time the provider is requesting that this order start.

columns.name: DURATION
columns.description: This is the length of time in days the provider requests that this orderlast.

columns.name: REQUESTED_STOP_DATE_TIME
columns.description: This is the Date/Time the provider is requesting that this order stop.

columns.name: UD_IV_PROMPT
columns.description: This field will be used during the finishing process to determine if theuser should be prompted whether they wish to finish the order as an IV orUnit Dose order.

columns.name: DOSE
columns.description: This is the numeric dosage for the order. It will be combined with theUNIT field to show the dosage ordered.  For a dosage of 325MG, 325 wouldbe stored here.

columns.name: UNIT
columns.description: This is the field which contains the unit for the numeric dosage.  Thecombination of these two fields gives you the dosage ordered for thisorder.  For a dosage of 325MG, MG would be stored here.

columns.name: SI_FLAG
columns.description: This flag controls whether the user administering this order in BCMA willhave the Special Instructions displayed in a pop-up box.

columns.name: OPI_FLAG
columns.description: This flag controls whether the user administering this order in BCMAwill have the Other Print Info displayed in a pop-up box.

columns.name: FLAGGED
columns.description: This indicates that this order has been flagged for clarification.

columns.name: ORDERS_FILE_PARENT_ORDER
columns.description: This is the parent of a CPRS order that may have a parent/childrelationship in CPRS

columns.name: APPOINTMENT_DATE_TIME
columns.description: This is the date and time of the appointment this order is being placedfor.

columns.name: REQUESTED_IV_LIMITATION
columns.description: This is the length of time to administer, or the total volume to administer, for IV fluid orders. The value may be in ML or CC formilliliters, L for liters, D for days, or H for hours.

columns.name: IV_TYPE_CATEGORY
columns.description: This field contains the category of the order's IV TYPE.  The IV TYPE CATEGORY will be 'C' (Continuous) for orders with an IV TYPEof Admixture, Hyperal, Non-Intermittent Syringe, or Chemotherapy with a CHEMOTHERAPY TYPE of Admixture, Hyperal, or Non-Intermittent Syringe. The IV TYPE CATEGORY will be 'I' (Intermittent) for orders with an IV TYPE of Piggyback, Intermittent Syringe, or Chemotherapy with a CHEMOTHERAPY TYPE of Piggyback or Intermittent Syringe.

columns.name: MOST_RECENT_FLAG_COMMENT
columns.description: MOST_RECENT_FLAG_COMMENT

columns.name: LABELS_PER_DAY
columns.description: The number of IV labels needed each day. If populated, this value will override the system-calculated number of labels.

columns.name: SPECIAL_INSTRUCTIONS_(LONG)
columns.description: This is any special instructions (using abbreviations whenever possible) needed for this order.  This would include the physician's reason for ordering a PRN.  The abbreviations and expansions from the MEDICATION INSTRUCTIONS file are utilized.

columns.name: OTHER_PRINT_INFO_(LONG)
columns.description: For use by Pharmacy to print additional information on IV labels andreports. This field is very similar to the REMARKS field except that OTHERINFO is shown on the label and the IV REPORTS.

columns.name: DURATION_OF_ADMINISTRATION
columns.description: This is the period of time that a Medication Requiring Removal must remainon the patient prior to removal.

columns.name: REMOVE_TIMES
columns.description: This is the set of removal times for this order.

columns.name: REMOVE_PERIOD_(IN_MINUTES)
columns.description: Period of time in minutes calculated using the Duration of Administration and the Administration times.  Only entered via PSJ OE.

columns.name: BCMA_PROMPT_FOR_REMOVAL_FLAG
columns.description: Orderable Item Prompt for Removal flag captured at order time.DO NOT EDIT!

columns.name: EXTERNAL_RX_#
columns.description: This is used to track the external Prescription number when the record ismigrated from an outside system.

entities.description: This is the medication ordered for the patient.

columns.name: AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_DISPENSE_DRUG_IEN
columns.description: Unique identifier for the AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_DISPENSE_DRUG file.

columns.name: AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_IEN
columns.description: FK to AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS

columns.name: DISPENSE_DRUG
columns.description: This is the medication that will actually be dispensed for this order.An order may have more than one dispense drug.

columns.name: UNITS_PER_DOSE
columns.description: This is the number of UNITS (tablets, capsules, etc.) to be dispensed as aDOSE for this order.  The literals '1/2' and '1/4' may be entered.  If thereis no entry, it is assumed to be ONE (1).                         ** PLEASE NOTE **  If a doctor prescribes 30 ml's of a medication that is usually dispensedand administered as 60 ml's, the correct UNITS PER DOSE would be 1/2 (or.5), NOT 30 ml's.  (30 ml's would be entered into the DOSAGE ORDERED field.)  If the UNITS PER DOSE ordered is a variable amount (1-2 tab.), it issuggested that the maximum amount be entered into this field and the amountordered noted either in the DOSAGE ORDERED or SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS fields.

columns.name: INACTIVE_DATE
columns.description: This is the date that this dispense drug will no longer be dispensed forthis order.  Once an order becomes active, dispense drugs cannot be deleted.

entities.description: This field will contain the narrative portion of the OBX segmentsent from OE/RR when an order check occurs.

columns.name: AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_ORDER_CHECKS_IEN
columns.description: Unique identifier for the AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_ORDER_CHECKS file.

columns.name: AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_IEN
columns.description: FK to AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS

columns.name: ORDER_CHECK_NARRATIVE
columns.description: This field will contain the narrative portion of the OBX segmentsent from OE/RR when an order check occurs.

columns.name: OVERRIDING_PROVIDER
columns.description: This field will contain the name of the provider who over-rode theorder check.  It comes as a part of the OBX segment from OE/RR.

columns.name: OVERRIDING_REASON
columns.description: OVERRIDING_REASON

entities.description: This multiple contains the data that relates to the renewal of an order.

columns.name: AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_LAST_RENEW_IEN
columns.description: Unique identifier for the AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_LAST_RENEW file.

columns.name: AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_IEN
columns.description: FK to AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS

columns.name: LAST_RENEW
columns.description: This is the date/time the order was renewed.

columns.name: RENEWED_BY
columns.description: This is the person who renewed the order.

columns.name: PREVIOUS_PROVIDER
columns.description: This is the name of the provider responsible for the prior order.

columns.name: PREVIOUS_STOP_DATE_TIME
columns.description: This is the stop date/time of the prior order.

entities.description: This is a record of the actions that have taken place on the order.Actionsinclude EDIT, RENEWAL, CANCELLATION, and FINISH. Stored with the action isthe date and time the action took place and the user who took the action.If the action is an edit, the data in the field edited prior to the editis also stored.

columns.name: AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_ACTIVITY_LOG_IEN
columns.description: Unique identifier for the AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_ACTIVITY_LOG file.

columns.name: AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_IEN
columns.description: FK to AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS

columns.name: DATE
columns.description: This is the date and time the activity took place.

columns.name: USER
columns.description: This is the user taking the action on the order.

columns.name: ACTION
columns.description: This is the activity that has taken place on the order.

columns.name: FIELD
columns.description: This is the field that was changed due to the activity.

columns.name: OLD_DATA
columns.description: This is the previous data that was in the field that was changed.

entities.description: Interventions logged during Inpatient Order Entry in response to drug-drugor drug-allergy order checks. Only interventions associated with a specific Inpatient Order will be stored with that order.

columns.name: AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_INTERVENTION_IEN
columns.description: Unique identifier for the AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_INTERVENTION file.

columns.name: AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_IEN
columns.description: FK to AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS

columns.name: INTERVENTION
columns.description: Pharmacy Interventions logged during Inpatient Order Entry in response to or drug-allergy order checks. Only interventions associated with aspecific Inpatient Order will be stored with that order.

columns.name: ACCEPTED_DATE_TIME
columns.description: The Date/Time the Intervention is logged in Inpatient Order Entry.

entities.description: The additive in the IV.  This looks at the IV ADDITIVES file (52.6).

columns.name: AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_ADDITIVE_IEN
columns.description: Unique identifier for the AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_ADDITIVE file.

columns.name: AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_IEN
columns.description: FK to AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS

columns.name: ADDITIVE
columns.description: The additive selected as part of the IV order.  This entry is a pointer to the ADDITIVES file (52.6).

columns.name: STRENGTH
columns.description: 'STRENGTH' is the amount of an additive to be used in the manufacturingof the IV order. NOTE! You will be expected to use the strength units thatwere previously defined within the IV ADDITIVE file (52.6) for each additive. For example, if the DRUG UNITS field of the IV ADDITIVES file specifies the units for ampicillin to be in grams, it would be incorrect to enter 500 for a half-gram dose. Enter 0.5 instead.

columns.name: BOTTLE
columns.description: This is the bottle number (or numbers, separated by commas) in which this additive will be included for this IV order. If this field is blank, it means that the additive will be included in all bottles.

entities.description: Solution in the IV.  Points to the IV SOLUTIONS file (52.7).

columns.name: AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_SOLUTION_IEN
columns.description: Unique identifier for the AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_SOLUTION file.

columns.name: AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS_IEN
columns.description: FK to AU_NON-VERIFIED_ORDERS

columns.name: SOLUTION
columns.description: The solution entered as part of the specified IV order.

columns.name: VOLUME
columns.description: The volume of this solution in MLs. Only numeric values may be enteredin this field.  The total volume of the IV order is sum of solution'svolumes.

entities.description: This file holds, for each patient, information that is typically ofinterest only to the pharmacy.  This should be noted when merging patientrecords and deleting the 'old' record from the patient file.  That processdoes not delete the corresponding pharmacy patient file entry. This file is also shared with inpatient pharmacy and promises to become avery central file to the pharmacy.

columns.name: AU_PHARMACY_PATIENT_IEN
columns.description: Unique identifier for the AU_PHARMACY_PATIENT file.

columns.name: NUMBER
columns.description: This allows users to select entries by the internal number.

columns.name: NAME
columns.description: This is the name of a patient that has some type of pharmacy order.

columns.name: CAP
columns.description: This field is used to indicate if safety caps are to be issued to patient.

columns.name: MAIL
columns.description: This field is used to:A) Determine whether this patient's Rx's are to be sent to the CMOP, orretained for local distribution. If 2-4 are selected, none of thispatient's Rx's will be transmitted to the CMOP.B) Select what the mail priority is.  The CMOP choices are limited to (0)REGULAR and (1) CERTIFIED. Local mail may be designated (3) LOCAL -REGULAR or (4) LOCAL - CERTIFIED. The 'DO NOT MAIL' code (2) may be usedto ensure that the patient's Rx's are not mailed.

columns.name: DIALYSIS_PATIENT
columns.description: This field is used to indicate if the patient is in dialysis.

columns.name: MAIL_STATUS_EXPIRATION_DATE
columns.description: This field places a time limit on the 'Do Not Mail', 'Local - RegularMail' and 'Local - Certified Mail' conditions in the 'MAIL' field.If a date is placed in this field and the software detects that the datethe Rx is processed is greater than the date in the field (past theexpired date) a default value of 'Regular Mail' will be assumed for the'MAIL' field.  NOTE: The actual value of the 'MAIL' field will not be changed by thesoftware, but can only be modified by a user editing the 'MAIL' field.

columns.name: FIRST_SERVICE_DATE
columns.description: This is the login date of the first order for pharmacy services.

columns.name: ACTUAL_HISTORICAL_FLAG
columns.description: The purpose of this field is to indicate whether the FIRST SERVICE DATE field was populated with actual or historical data.  Actual indicates the field was populated when the first pharmacy service was filed.  Historical indicates the field was populated by the conversion routine.

columns.name: NARRATIVE
columns.description: This is notable information about the patient that pertains to pharmacy.

columns.name: PATIENT_STATUS
columns.description: This field is used to indicate a default patient status.

columns.name: COMMUNITY_NURSING_HOME
columns.description: This field is used to indicate if the patient resides within a communitynursing home.

columns.name: NURSING_HOME_CONTRACT
columns.description: This field is used to indicate if the patient has a nursing home contract.

columns.name: LAST_DATE_OF_CONTRACT
columns.description: This field is used to indicate the last date of the nursing home contract.

columns.name: RESPITE_PATIENT_START_DATE
columns.description: This field is used to indicate the start date of respite care.

columns.name: RESPITE_PATIENT_END_DATE
columns.description: This field is used to indicate the end date of respite care.

columns.name: ACTIVE_SCRIPTS
columns.description: This field is used to indicate active prescriptions.

columns.name: RX_UPDATE
columns.description: This field is used to indicate if the patient's medications have beenupdated in the CPRS orders file.If the field is 0, nothing has been updated, 1 indicates the initial datamovement is complete, and 2 indicates the Backfill to CPRS is complete.

columns.name: CLOZAPINE_REGISTRATION_NUMBER
columns.description: This is the patient's authorization number assigned by national data base.

columns.name: CLOZAPINE_STATUS
columns.description: This is the patient's clozapine treatment status.

columns.name: DATE_OF_LAST_CLOZAPINE_RX
columns.description: This is the date of the patient's last clozapine prescription.

columns.name: DEMOGRAPHICS_SENT
columns.description: This indicates whether patient demographic data has been sent tothe national database.

columns.name: RESPONSIBLE_PROVIDER
columns.description: This is the physician responsible for the patient's clozaril treatment.

columns.name: REGISTRATION_DATE
columns.description: This field is used to enter the date of registration.

columns.name: UD_DEFAULT_STOP_DATE_TIME
columns.description: This is date used as a default value for the STOP DATE/TIME of Unit Doseorders during the order entry and renewal processes, if the correspondingsite parameter is turned on.  The order entry and renewal processes willsometimes change this date.

columns.name: UD_PROVIDER
columns.description: This is the latest provider for this patient, used as a default valuein order entry.

columns.name: UD_LAST_ADMISSION_DATE
columns.description: This is the last admission date for this patient.

columns.name: UD_LAST_TRANSFER_DATE
columns.description: This is the last transfer date for this patient.

columns.name: UD_LAST_DISCHARGE_DATE
columns.description: This is the last discharge date for this patient.

columns.name: UD_EXP_UP-DATE
columns.description: This is a date used to update expired orders.  (Internal)

columns.name: UD_HOLD_FLAG
columns.description: This is an internal flag set when all of the patient's orders havebeen placed on hold.If '2', all of a patient's Unit Dose AND IV orders were placed on holdautomatically by the package.

columns.name: UD_DISCHARGE_FLAG
columns.description: This is an internal flag set when a patient is first found to have beendischarged.  It is set so that Inpatient Meds does not try to cancel thepatient's orders every time the patient is accessed while discharged.

columns.name: COMMENTS
columns.description: This is used for temporary storage of data by the Unit Dose package.The data is deleted before and after each use!

columns.name: HOLD_REASON
columns.description: This is an explanation of why this patient's orders are being placed onhold.  This explanation will show on the patient's Unit Dose profile.

columns.name: *LAST_UD_ORDER_CONVERTED_TO_V4
columns.description: This is the last Unit Dose order converted for use with version 4 of theInpatient Medications package.THIS SHOULD NOT BE EDITED.  Editing could result in corrupted data andpossibly medication administration errors.

columns.name: INPATIENT_NARRATIVE
columns.description: This field stores the Inpatient pharmacy narrative for the patient.

columns.name: *UD_STOP_DATE
columns.description: This field is used by the UNIT DOSE PHARMACY package.  It is NOTto be entered into anywhere else!

columns.name: *NO._OF_IV_ORDERS
columns.description: *NO._OF_IV_ORDERS

columns.name: *LAST_ADMISSION_NUMBER
columns.description: This field is updated by the IV PACKAGE every time action is taken onthis particular patient.  This piece will have two pieces of informationon it.  The first piece ('-' is the delimiter) is the current admissionsnumber, and the second piece is the discharge date for this admissionsnumber.  This field is used for determining whether or not to DC IV ORDERSdue to ADMISSIONS or DISCHARGE.

columns.name: *LAST_SERVICE
columns.description: This piece is updated by the IV PACKAGE every time this particular patienthas any 'IV ACTION'.  This piece represents the service of the last wardthat this patient was in.  It is a set of codes that was taken from the ADTpackage.  This field is used to determine whether or not to DC IV ORDERSdue to SERVICE transfer.

columns.name: *LAST_INTERWARD_TRANSFER
columns.description: This field is updated by the IV PACKAGE every time this particular patienthas any 'IV ACTION'.  This field represents the last INTERWARD TRANSFERNUMBER for the LAST ADMISSION NUMBER.  This field is used to determinewhether or not to DC IV ORDERS due to WARD TRANSFER.ORDERS due to SERVICE transfer.

columns.name: *LAST_IV_ORDER_CONVERTED_(4.0)
columns.description: This is the last IV order for a patient that had it's data converted tothe New Person file (200).

columns.name: _CONVERSION_COMPLETED?
columns.description: This field contains a 1 if the conversion to the patient's orders forversion 5.0 has  completed.  It contains a 2 if the conversion to thepatient's orders for Pharmacy Ordering Enhancement (POE) has completed.  It contains a 3 if the patient's IV orders existed prior to BCMA V.2.0 has updated the Verifying Pharmacist field.

columns.name: OTHER_LANGUAGE_PREFERENCE
columns.description: This field is used to identify patients who have another language preferencefor printing medication instructions on bottle labels.

columns.name: PMI_LANGUAGE_PREFERENCE
columns.description: This field will be used to determine the default language preference forprinting the PMI sheets at the CMOPs.

entities.description: This subfile contains IV order information for any given patient.A separate IV order file does not exist. This isn't the same design as outpatient pharmacy -- which does contain a separate file forprescriptions.

columns.name: AU_PHARMACY_PATIENT_IV_IEN
columns.description: Unique identifier for the AU_PHARMACY_PATIENT_IV file.

columns.name: AU_PHARMACY_PATIENT_IEN
columns.description: FK to AU_PHARMACY_PATIENT

columns.name: ORDER_NUMBER
columns.description: Order Number for IV drugs administered to this patient.

columns.name: START_DATE_TIME
columns.description: This is the date and time the order is to begin. This package initiallyassigns the START DATE/TIME to the closest administration time or nextadmin. time or NOW depends on the value of the DEFAULT START DATECALCULATION field in the WARD PARAMETERS file. START DATE/TIME may not be entered prior to 7 days from the order's LOGIN DATE.

columns.name: STOP_DATE_TIME
columns.description: This is the date and time the order is to end.

columns.name: TYPE
columns.description: Type of IV - 'A' for Admixture, 'C' for chemotherapy, 'H' for Hyperal, 'P'for Piggyback, and 'S' for Syringe.

columns.name: PROVIDER
columns.description: Person who authorized the prescription.

columns.name: INFUSION_RATE
columns.description: The rate at which the IV is to be administered.  This value, togetherwith the total volume of the hyperal or the admixture type, is used todetermine the time covered by one bag; hence the system can predict thebags needed during a specified time of coverage.  This field is free textfor IVPB's.  For LVP's you must enter a number representing the infusionrate.  You may also specify the # of bags per day needed, which willbecome the default number of LABELS PER DAY.  Example: 125 = 125 ml/hr (IV system will calculate bags needed per day)        125@2 = 125 ml/hr with 2 labels per day    TITRATE@1 = TITRATE with 1 label per day The format of this field is either a number only or [FREE TEXT@NUMBER OF LABELS PER DAY]. Note:  If an administration time(s) is defined, the number of labels willreflect the administration time(s) for the IVPB type orders.For example:  One administration time of 12:00 is specified.  The infusionrate is entered as 125@3.  Only 1 label will print.

columns.name: SCHEDULE
columns.description: You may enter a standard schedule here or non-standard schedule.  If astandard schedule is entered, the doses will be given at the administrationtime(s). If a non-standard schedule is entered, and no administrationtimes are entered, the doses will be given at time intervals past the startdate/time of the IV order.    TID = (09-17-21) doses will be given at admin. times.    Q5H = (300 minutes) doses will be given every 300 minutes.The format of this field is [SCHEDULEspaceFREETEXTspaceFREETEXT] and 1-70characters.

columns.name: REMARKS
columns.description: This field is not shown on the IV labels, but is shown on some of theIV reports.

columns.name: ADMINISTRATION_TIMES
columns.description: Enter the times that this order will be given separated by a '-'.  Theadministration times have to be entered in ascending order.  Each administration time must be at least two characters long or fourcharacters long.  Example: '03-07-11-15-19-23' or '0730-1130'.  Administration times are REQUIRED for STANDARD schedules but are NOT REQUIRED for NON-STANDARD schedules.

columns.name: LAST_FILL
columns.description: Last time the prescription was filled.

columns.name: LAST_QTY_FILLED
columns.description: Quantity of last filled prescription.

columns.name: SCHEDULE_INTERVAL
columns.description: Interval between administrations of IV

columns.name: LOGIN_DATE_TIME
columns.description: This is the date and time the order was entered.

columns.name: IV_ROOM
columns.description: IV room where IV was prepared for administration.

columns.name: *ENTRY_CODE
columns.description: This is the user who entered the order into the system.

columns.name: CUMULATIVE_DOSES
columns.description: Cumulative doses of IV for patient.

columns.name: ORIGINAL_WARD
columns.description: This is the ward where the patient was located when the order was created.

columns.name: VERIFYING_NURSE
columns.description: This is the nurse who acknowledged (through OE/RR) the order, or the latesaction taken on the order.

columns.name: DATE_VERIFIED_BY_NURSE
columns.description: This is the date the order was acknowledged (through OE/RR) by the nurse.

columns.name: OTHER_PRINT_INFO
columns.description: This field is very similar to the REMARKS field except that OTHER INFOis shown on the label and the IV REPORTS.

columns.name: STATUS
columns.description: Status of order. Enter one of following codes: A for active, H for hold,R for renewed, D for discontinued, E for expired, P for purge, O for on call, N for nonverified.

columns.name: *DOSAGE_ORDERED
columns.description: This is the dosage prescribed by the physician.

columns.name: *IV_ORDERED
columns.description: This field is used only for orders entered through the OE/RR interface.If a hyperal is ordered, this field will contain 'HYPERAL IV ORDER'.  Ifan admixture is ordered, it will contain the free text drug name entered, and may be from 1 to 40 characters long.  If a piggyback is ordered it will be null, as the drug entered will be an entry in the additives file, and is stored in the ADDITIVES sub-file (55.02) for the order.

columns.name: *SPECIAL_INSTRUCTIONS
columns.description: This field contains any special instructions or messages appropriate forthis IV order.  This field may only be edited when entering an order throughthe OE/RR package, and will only be displayed when viewing the order untilthe order has been verified.

columns.name: WARD
columns.description: If the IV is not a outpatient IV, this field will be a pointer to theward file 42. If the IV is a outpatient IV, this field will contain a .5

columns.name: TOTAL_IV'S_ADMINISTERED
columns.description: This is the total number of doses of this IV order which have beenadministered to the patient.

columns.name: CHEMOTHERAPY_TYPE
columns.description: A chemotherapy IV order may be one of three types: admixture, piggyback,or syringe.  The type of chemotherapy IV must be identified as one of thesetypes, so the system will know what kinds of questions to ask in order toproperly complete this order.

columns.name: SYRINGE_SIZE
columns.description: Enter the size of the syringe which is to be used to administer this IV.

columns.name: INTERMITTENT_SYRINGE
columns.description: A syringe IV order may be continuous or intermittent.  If a syringe typeis continuous (not intermittent), the same order entry procedure will befollowed as if a hyperal or admixture is being entered.  If a syringe orderis to be intermittent, the same order entry method as the piggback typewill be followed.

columns.name: DC_DATE
columns.description: This is the date the IV order selected was discontinued.

columns.name: ORDERS_FILE_ENTRY
columns.description: This value matches this IV order to its entry in the Order file.

columns.name: ATZERO
columns.description: This field is a 1 or a null. It will be a 1 if the IV order isintermittent and a schedule was entered in the form SCHEDULE@0.Notice the 'NO space' in the input. When I see a schedule enteredin this form, I set this field to one. A 1 means that the user wantsto see these order on the ward list and manufacturing list with0 doses due. They will not get scheduled labels for these ordersunless they update the ward list first. They can get these labelsfrom individual order print. This is a 'print on demand function'just like entering INFUSION RATE@0 for continuous orders.

columns.name: PREVIOUS_ORDER
columns.description: If an action is taken on an order that causes a new order to be created,this will contain a code identifying the previous order.

columns.name: FOLLOWING_ORDER
columns.description: If an action is taken on an order that causes a new order to be created,this will contain a code identifying the status and location of the neworder.

columns.name: PROVIDER_COMMENTS
columns.description: This contains any comments about the order that the provider needsto pass along to pharmacy or ward personnel. This field may only beedited using OE/RR options.

columns.name: ORIGINAL_STOP_DATE
columns.description: When an action is taken on an order that causes the order's originalstop date to be changed, the original stop date is stored in this field.

columns.name: *PRIMARY_DRUG
columns.description: Used to store the primary drug entered through OE/RR for Inpatient Medication IV orders. If the order entered is an Inpatient Medication IV order, the primary drug is taken from the first additive or solution entered. The primary drug will be displayed for this order type on theOE/RR Review Orders screen and other displays used by the clinician.

columns.name: *MED_ROUTE
columns.description: This is the route of administration for this order. This is not requiredfor IV Fluid orders.

columns.name: OERR_HOLD_FLAG
columns.description: If an IV order is placed on hold using OE/RR options, the hold may onlybe removed using OE/RR options.

columns.name: AUTO_DC
columns.description: This is used to determine if an order was auto-discontinued due to a patient movement. Only orders that were discontinued in this way maybe reinstated by pharmacy. When reinstated, the status will becomeactive, and the original stop date will be used.

columns.name: REASON_ORDER_CREATED
columns.description: This is used to show the method used to create this order.what actions may be taken on the order.

columns.name: REASON_FOR_FOLLOWING_ORDER
columns.description: This is used to determine the action taken which caused the creation ofthe following order.

columns.name: MAR_LABEL_DATE
columns.description: This is the date and time the latest MAR label for this order was created.

columns.name: MAR_LABEL_REASON
columns.description: This is the last activity to take place on the order that created a label record.

columns.name: ORDERABLE_ITEM
columns.description: This is the Orderable Item associated with the order. If the order isa unit dose order, all dispense drugs entered must be matched to theorder's primary drug. If the order is an IV, at lest one of theadditives or solutions entered must match the orderable item.

columns.name: DOSAGE_ORDERED
columns.description: This is the amount of the medication the patient is to receive as one dosefor this order. This should be an amount with a unit of measure, such as'500MG' or '50cc'. THIS SHOULD NOT BE THE NUMBER OF TABLETS, ETC.

columns.name: MED_ROUTE
columns.description: This is the route of administration for this order. This is not requiredfor IV Fluid orders.

columns.name: INSTRUCTIONS
columns.description: INSTRUCTIONS

columns.name: PRIORITY
columns.description: This field contains the priority of the order that was received from OERR.

columns.name: ENTRY_BY
columns.description: This field contains the pointer value for the person entered the IV order.

columns.name: CLINIC
columns.description: CLINIC

columns.name: NATURE_OF_ORDER

columns.name: ORDER_NUMBER
columns.description: This is the record number of the order.

columns.name: PRIORITY
columns.description: This field contains the priority of the order that was received from OERR.

columns.name: ORIGINAL_ORDER_NUMBER
columns.description: This is the original number of the order from file 53.1.

columns.name: PATIENT_NAME
columns.description: This is the patient for which the medication has been ordered.

columns.name: PROVIDER
columns.description: This is the prescribing physician's name.

columns.name: MED_ROUTE
columns.description: This is the route of administration for this medication. If a corresponding abbreviation is found for this route in the MEDICATION ROUTES file, that abbreviation is printed on the various reports in this package.

columns.name: TYPE
columns.description: This identifies the type of medication ordered.

columns.name: SELF_MED
columns.description: This should contain a `1' or (`YES') if this medication is to beadministered by the patient to himself.

columns.name: HOSPITAL_SUPPLIED_SELF_MED
columns.description: This should contain a `1' (or `YES') if this medication is to be a`SELF MED' and this site's pharmacy is to supply the medication.  Thisis only asked if the user enters `YES' (or `1') to the SELF MED prompt.If the SELF MED prompt is ever edited to show `NO' (or `0'), this field isautomatically deleted.

columns.name: SCHEDULE_TYPE
columns.description: This describes the type of schedule for the dispensing of themedication(s) that make up the order.  PRE-OP orders are usually considered to be ON-CALL orders, and ordersdispensed as MUTLI-DOSE CONTAINERS are usually considered to be FILL ONREQUEST orders.

columns.name: SPECIAL_INSTRUCTIONS
columns.description: This is any special instructions (using abbreviations whenever possible)needed for this order.  This would include the physician's reason forordering a PRN.  This field utilizes the abbreviations and expansionsfrom the MEDICATION INSTRUCTIONS file.

columns.name: ORIGINAL_WARD
columns.description: This is the ward where the patient was located when the order was created.

columns.name: START_DATE_TIME
columns.description: This is the date and time the order is to begin.  This package initially assigns the START DATE/TIME to the closest administration time or next admin. time or NOW depends on the value of the DEFAULT START DATE CALCULATION field in the INPATIENT WARD PARAMETERS.  START DATE/TIME may not be entered prior to 7 days from the order's LOGIN DATE.

columns.name: DAY_LIMIT
columns.description: This is number of days this order is to last.

columns.name: DOSE_LIMIT
columns.description: This is the number of times the medication is to be administered.

columns.name: *UNITS_PER_DOSE
columns.description: This is the number of UNITS (tablets, capsules, etc.) to be dispensed as aDOSE for this order.  The literals '1/2' and '1/4' may be entered.  If thereis no entry, it is assumed to be ONE (1).                         ** PLEASE NOTE **  If a doctor prescribes 30 ml's of a medication that is usually dispensedand administered as 60 ml's, the correct UNITS PER DOSE would be 1/2 (or.5), NOT 30 ml's.  (30 ml's would be entered into the DOSAGE ORDERED field.)  If the UNITS PER DOSE ordered is a variable amount (1-2 tab.), it issuggested that the maximum amount be entered into this field and the amountordered noted either in the DOSAGE ORDERED or SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS fields.

columns.name: *PRE-EXCHANGE_UNITS
columns.description: This is the number of actual units required for this order until thenext cart exchange.

columns.name: COMMENTS
columns.description: This is a word processing field that is purely informational.  Thisfield only shows on the expanded view of the order.

columns.name: VERIFYING_NURSE
columns.description: This is the nurse who verified the order, or the latest action takenon the order.

columns.name: DATE_VERIFIED_BY_NURSE
columns.description: This is the date the order was verified by the nurse.

columns.name: VERIFYING_PHARMACIST
columns.description: This is the pharmacist who verified the order.

columns.name: DATE_VERIFIED_BY_PHARMACIST
columns.description: This is the date the order was verified by the pharmacist.

columns.name: PHYSICIAN
columns.description: This is the physician who signed off on the order.

columns.name: DATE_VERIFIED_BY_PHYSICIAN
columns.description: This is the date the physician signed off on the order.

columns.name: CLERK
columns.description: (Not currently used.)

columns.name: DATE_ENTERED_BY_CLERK
columns.description: (Not currently used.)

columns.name: *SOLUTION
columns.description: (Not currently used.)

columns.name: PREVIOUS_STOP_DATE_TIME
columns.description: This is used to store the original stop date when it is changed dueto the order being cancelled.  This allows the order to be reinstated.

columns.name: SCHEDULE
columns.description: This is the frequency (ONLY) by which the doses are to be administered.  Several forms of entry are acceptable, such as Q6H, 09-12-15, STAT, QOD, and MO-WE-FR@AD (where MO-WE-FR are days of the week, and AD is the admin times.) The schedule will show on the MAR, labels, etc. If the letters PRN are found as part of the schedule, no admin times will print on the MAR or labels, and the PICK LIST will always show a count of zero (0). Avoid using notation such as W/F (with food) or WM (with meals) in the schedule as it may cause erroneous calculations.  That information should be entered into the SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS. When using the MO-WE-FR@AD schedule, please remember that this type of schedule will not work properly without the '@' character and at least one admin. time, and that at least the first two letters of each weekday entered is needed.

columns.name: ORDER_DATE
columns.description: This is the date the order was entered into the computer.  The packageenters this date automatically when the order is transcribed.

columns.name: LOG-IN_DATE
columns.description: This is the date (to the second) the order was entered.

columns.name: STATUS
columns.description: This is the status of the order.

columns.name: *UNITS_CALLED_FOR
columns.description: This is the total number of units to be dispensed for this medicationas calculated by the package.

columns.name: STOP_DATE_TIME
columns.description: This is the date and time the order will automatically expire.  Thispackage initially calculates a default stop date, depending on the SITEPARAMETERS.

columns.name: *TOTAL_RETURNS
columns.description: This is the total number units returned for this medication over thelife of the order.

columns.name: *UNITS_ACTUALLY_DISPENSED
columns.description: This is the number of units of this medication actually dispensed asentered by the pharmacist.

columns.name: *RETURNS
columns.description: This is the number of units returned of this medication from the patient'scassette upon the termination of this order.

columns.name: *TOTALS_UNITS_DISPENSED
columns.description: This is the total number of units actually dispensed for this order,including any EXTRA UNIT DISPENSED, and PRE-EXCHANGE NEEDS.

columns.name: ADMIN_TIMES
columns.description: This is the times of the day the medication is to be administered.  Thispackage initially assigns a default set of ADMIN TIMES when a STANDARDSCHEDULE is entered into the SCHEDULE prompt.

columns.name: FREQUENCY_(IN_MINUTES)
columns.description: This is either a code or the number of minutes between the times themedication is to be administered.

columns.name: RENEWAL
columns.description: This is an internal flag, set when the order is marked to be renewed.

columns.name: RENEWAL_USER
columns.description: This is the user who marked the order to be renewed.

columns.name: DATE_RENEWAL_MARKED
columns.description: This is the date this order was renewed or marked for renewal.

columns.name: MARKED_CANCELLED
columns.description: This is an internal flag set when the order is marked for cancellation.

columns.name: MARKED_CANCELLED_USER
columns.description: This is the user who marked the order for cancellation.

columns.name: DATE_MARKED_CANCELLED
columns.description: This is the date that the order was marked for cancellation.

columns.name: AUTO_CANCELLED_FLAG
columns.description: This is an internal flag looked at by the UNIT DOSE package to determineif this order was automatically cancelled by the package because the patientwas newly admitted, transferred, or discharged (or deceased).  If this flag is on (1), the order may be reinstated within 72 hours of its cancellation.

columns.name: PV_FLAG
columns.description: This is an internal flag set whenever a pharmacist verifies the order.

columns.name: NV_FLAG
columns.description: This is an internal flag set whenever a nurse verifies the order.

columns.name: LABEL_DATE
columns.description: This is the date the last label record was created for the order.

columns.name: LABEL_REASON
columns.description: This is the last activity to take place on the order that created alabel record.

columns.name: *TOTALS_EXTRA_UNITS_DISPENSED
columns.description: This is the total number of extra units dispensed for this order overthe entire life of the order.

columns.name: *EXTRA_UNITS_DISPENSED
columns.description: This is the number of units dispensed outside of the normal dispensingprocess (pick list).

columns.name: HOLD_FLAG
columns.description: This is an internal number set whenever the order is placed on HOLD,or marked to be placed on hold.

columns.name: HOLD_USER
columns.description: This is the user who placed the order on hold, or marked the order to beplaced on hold.

columns.name: HOLD_DATE
columns.description: This is the date the order was placed on hold, or marked to be placedon hold.

columns.name: HOLD_STATUS
columns.description: This is the previous status of the order, updated when the order isplaced on HOLD.  This allows the return of the previous status when theorder is taken off of hold.

columns.name: OERR_HOLD_FLAG

columns.name: OFF_HOLD_FLAG
columns.description: This is an internal flag set when an order is taken off of hold, ormarked to be taken off of hold.

columns.name: OFF_HOLD_USER

columns.name: OFF_HOLD_DATE

columns.name: *TOTAL_PRE-EXCHANGE_UNITS

columns.name: PURGE_FLAG
columns.description: This is an internal flag set when the order is due to be purged (deleted).This is actually the patient's discharge date, to allow the use of the'AUDDD' x-ref.

columns.name: *SIG
columns.description: This is the provider's exact instructions for this order's medicationand its administration.

columns.name: ORDERS_FILE_ENTRY
columns.description: This is the pointer value of the corresponding entry in the ORDERSfile (100) when the order is entered into OE/RR.

columns.name: MERGED_PATIENT
columns.description: If the order is moved from one patient to another, because patients arebeing merged, there will be data here.  The data will be in the form ofanother patient's internal record number concatenated with either a `T' (ifthe order has been moved to the other patient), or an `F' (if the came FROMthe other patient).

columns.name: LAST_WARD
columns.description: This is the last ward the patient was located when the order expiredor was discontinued.  This is automatically updated by the Unit Dosepackage when the package finds that the patient is first admitted orwhen the patient is found to have been transferred.  This allows anyreturns that are entered to be credited to the correct ward.

columns.name: 'NOT_TO_BE_GIVEN'_FLAG
columns.description: This is a flag that may be set for orders that have been discontinuedor expired only.  If the flag is set, the order cannot be renewed orreinstated.  This is to be set only through the package, and not throughVA FileMan.

columns.name: ORIGINAL_START_DATE_TIME
columns.description: This is the original start date/time of the order.  An entry isautomatically made here the first time the order is renewed.

columns.name: PROVIDER_COMMENTS
columns.description: This is any instructions or other comments entered by the provider ofthis order for this order.

columns.name: *PRIMARY_DRUG
columns.description: This is the primary drug associated with the order. If the order isa unit dose order all dispensed drugs entered must be matched to theorder's primary drug. If the order is an IV order at least one of theadditives or solutions entered must match the primary drug.

columns.name: *DOSAGE_ORDERED
columns.description: This is the amount of the medication the patient is to receive as onedose for this order.  This should be an amount with a unit of measure,such '500MG' or '50CC'.  THIS SHOULD NOT BE THE NUMBER OF TABLETS, ETC.

columns.name: REASON_ORDER_CREATED
columns.description: This is used to show the method used to create this order.

columns.name: PREVIOUS_ORDER
columns.description: If an action is taken on an order that causes a new order to be created,this will contain a code identifying the previous order.

columns.name: FOLLOWING_ORDER
columns.description: If an action is taken on an order that causes a new order to be created,this will contain a code identifying the order created.

columns.name: *NATURE_OF_ORDER
columns.description: This is the method the provider used to communicate to the user to enter(or take any other action) the order.

columns.name: REASON_FOR_FOLLOWING_ORDER
columns.description: If the order has been edited or renewed, this will contain the code corresponding to the action taken.

columns.name: ORDERABLE_ITEM
columns.description: This is the Orderable Item associated with the order. If the order isa unit dose order, all dispense drugs entered must be matched to theorder's primary drug. If the order is an IV, at lest one of theadditives or solutions entered must match the orderable item.

columns.name: DOSAGE_ORDERED
columns.description: This is the amount of the medication the patient is to receive as one dose for this order. This should be an amount with a unit of measure, such as '500MG' or '50cc'. THIS SHOULD NOT BE THE NUMBER OF TABLETS, ETC.

columns.name: NATURE_OF_ORDER
columns.description: This is the method the provider used to communicate to the user to enter(or take any other action) on the order.

columns.name: INSTRUCTIONS
columns.description: INSTRUCTIONS

columns.name: DOSE
columns.description: This is the numeric dosage for the order.  It will be combined with theUNIT field to show the dosage ordered.  For a dosage of 325MG, 325 wouldbe stored here.

columns.name: UNIT
columns.description: This is the field which contains the unit for the numeric dosage.  Thecombination of these two fields gives you the dosage ordered for thisorder.  For the doasge 325MG, MG would be stored here.

columns.name: SI_OPI_FLAG
columns.description: This flag controls whether the user administering this order in BCMA willhave the Special Instructions displayed in a pop-up box.

columns.name: BCMA_EXPIRED_FLAG
columns.description: This is an internal flag to indicate the order was expired at therequest of the Bar Code Medication Administration (BCMA) package. If theflag is set to 1, then BCMA requested Inpatient Medications expire theorder.  Only orders with the flag set to 1 can be reinstated by a BCMAreinstate request.

columns.name: FLAGGED
columns.description: This indicates that this order has been flagged for clarification.

columns.name: ORDERS_FILE_PARENT_ORDER
columns.description: This is the parent of an order that may have a parent/child relationship in CPRS.

columns.name: REQUESTED_DURATION
columns.description: The duration of an order as requested by the ordering clinician in CPRS.The duration is stored as one of the following upper case letters followedby an integer:  L - Months W - Weeks D - Days H - Hours M - Minutes S - Seconds Example: D6 = Six days.

The 'HP' is to display on the profile if theorder was placed on hold by provider through CPRS.

columns.name: REMOVE_TIMES

columns.name: REMOVE_PERIOD_(IN_MINUTES)

columns.name: FREE_TEXT_DOSAGE

columns.name: UNITS_PER_DOSE
columns.description: This is the number of UNITS (tablets, capsules, etc.) to be dispensed as aDOSE for this order.  The literals '1/2' and '1/4' may be entered.  If thereis no entry, it is assumed to be ONE (1).                         ** PLEASE NOTE **  If a doctor prescribes 30 ml's of a medication that is usually dispensedand administered as 60 ml's, the correct UNITS PER DOSE would be 1/2 (or.5), NOT 30 ml's.  (30 ml's would be entered into the DOSAGE ORDERED field.)  If the UNITS PER DOSE ordered is a variable amount (1-2 tab.), it issuggested that the maximum amount be entered into this field and the amountordered noted either in the DOSAGE ORDERED or SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS fields.

columns.name: PRE-EXCHANGE_UNITS

entities.description: This file is used to enter pharmacy interventions.Interventions in this file are records of occurrences where thepharmacist had to take some sort of action involving aparticular prescription or order.  A record would record thingslike the provider involved, why an intervention was necessary,what action was taken by the pharmacists.

columns.name: AU_APSP_INTERVENTION_IEN
columns.description: Unique identifier for the AU_APSP_INTERVENTION file.

columns.name: INTERVENTION_DATE
columns.description: This is the date that you recorded the intervention.You can enter any standard FileMan date input.ex. 2/5/90, Feb 5, 1990, etc.

columns.name: PATIENT
columns.description: You should enter the patient that you are intervening for.  You mayuse any of the normal ways you use to enter a prompt that asks fora patient. Ex. Lastname, Firstname MI. or ID#

columns.name: PROVIDER
columns.description: You should enter the name of the provider that prescribed this medication or treatment that you are intervening on.You may enter the provider's name or the provider's synonym.

columns.name: PHARMACIST
columns.description: You should enter the name of the pharmacist making theintervention and who will be doing the follow up withthe provider.

columns.name: DRUG
columns.description: If there is a drug involved in the intervention, enter the name of thedrug here.  This is a pointer to your local Drug file and you willonly be able to enter drugs that are in this file.

columns.name: INSTITUTED_BY
columns.description: This field is asking who initially brought up the need for anintervention.  You should enter a '?' to see your choices.The choices currently offered include : Pharmacy, Nursing, Provider,Patient or Family, and Other (to catch everybody else).

columns.name: INTERVENTION
columns.description: You are given a selection of 19 different types of interventions.  You should enter 1 of the choices.  Choices include: Inappropriate Drug, Incorrect Dose, Allergy, etc. If you would like to see a list of all your choices enter a '?' at the prompt.  If none of the selections really cover the reason for the intervention you should enter 'Other'.

columns.name: RECOMMENDATION
columns.description: This is the type of recommendation the pharmacist is goingto make to the provider. You can see the list of selectionsby entering a '?' at the prompt. Just as in previous fieldsif none of the selections cover the recommendation thepharmacist should enter an 'Other' at the prompt.

columns.name: WAS_PROVIDER_CONTACTED
columns.description: This field is used to record whether or not a provider wascontacted regarding the intervention.  In most cases aprovider will be contacted but if a pharmacy and a providerhave certain agreements about changing orders the provider maynot be contacted.

columns.name: PROVIDER_CONTACTED
columns.description: This field is used to record the name of a provider that was contacted if it is different from the provider who wrote the prescription or ordered the treatment.  It is a pointer to the New Person file and you should enter the provider here just as you would anyplace else.

columns.name: RECOMMENDATION_ACCEPTED
columns.description: This field is used to record whether your recommendation was accepted or rejected by the provider.

columns.name: AGREE_WITH_PROVIDER
columns.description: This field is used to record whether you agree with the providerif your recommendation was rejected.  This field will only be askedif the user answered 'No' to the Recommendation Accepted field.  Thepharmacist should answer either 'Yes' or 'No'.

columns.name: ORIGINATING_PACKAGE
columns.description: This field contains information about whether a intervention wasoriginated by the Outpatient Pharmacy or Inpatient Medicationssoftware.

columns.name: RX_#
columns.description: This field contains the prescription number involved in anintervention.  This field is filled by the routine called fordrug-drug interactions.

columns.name: DIVISION
columns.description: This is the pharmacy division involved in the intervention

columns.name: FINANCIAL_COST
columns.description: This field is used to estimate the savings due to this intervention.

columns.name: OTHER_FOR_INTERVENTION
columns.description: This field is used when a pharmacist has chosen 'Other' as theentry for the Intervention field.  This is a word processing fieldthat the pharmacist can then use to enter a Intervention Type thatwas not covered by the other selections of the Intervention field.The person making the entry will only be asked this field ifthey entered 'Other' in the Intervention field.

columns.name: OTHER_FOR_RECOMMENDATION
columns.description: This field is used to enter other recommedations if 'Other' is entered asa recommendation.

columns.name: REASON_FOR_INTERVENTION
columns.description: This field is used to enter a more detailed explantion of the intervention.

columns.name: ACTION_TAKEN
columns.description: This field is used to enter a more detailed explanation of the action taken.

columns.name: CLINICAL_IMPACT
columns.description: This field is used by the pharmacist if they want to document what theyfelt the clinical impact of the intervention is.

columns.name: FINANCIAL_IMPACT
columns.description: This field is used to to document if some type of financial impact isrelated to the intervention.
